rules.description: Legacy category for failures in explicit software security features.
A statement has no effect
Data provided remotely is used in this external API without sanitization, which could be a security risk.
Disabling or weakening CSRF protection may make the application vulnerable to a Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attack.
Credentials are hard coded in the source code of the application.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Using jinja2 templates with 'autoescape=False' can cause a cross-site scripting vulnerability.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
rules.description: Writing user input directly to a web page allows for a cross-site scripting vulnerability.
Cookies without the `HttpOnly` attribute set can be accessed by JS scripts, making them more vulnerable to XSS attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
rules.description: The built-in function 'input' is used which, in Python 2, can allow arbitrary code to be run.

rules.cwe_name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
rules.description: Calling super with something other than the enclosing class may cause incorrect object initialization.
